summary: Kerry Skora works in Indology and religious studies. Skora held posts at the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute and Hiram College, both attested in 2004.

Keshav Pandurang Jog (1925–2000) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Elphinstone College under R. P. Kangle and earned a PhD at the University of Mumbai (~1960–1965) under Hari Damodar Velankar, later serving at Deccan College (1980–1987).

Kevin A. Vose specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his BA from Bates College and his MA and PhD (2005) from the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional teacher Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa.

Kevin Buckelew is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College and Columbia University (PhD 2018 under Chün-fang Yü, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang), joining Northwestern University as Assistant Professor in 2018.

Kevin McGrath (born 1951) is a scholar of Indology. He held a post at Harvard University (attested 1998) and served as Professor of Religion, History and Human Sciences at George Washington University (attested 2016).

Kevin Vogelaar specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from SUNY New Paltz (BA), Fordham University (MA 2015–2018), and Tufts University (MA 2018–2020), holding curatorial and research posts at Fordham, Tufts, and the Armenian Museum of America.
Kexin Zheng is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Zheng is a PhD candidate at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).

Khakyab Dorje (1871–1922) was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Khenchen Tashi Özer, and others, and taught numerous students, including Kalu Rinpoche.
Kham Sum Zilnön Gyepa Dorjé studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Khammai Dhammasami (born 1965) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a DPhil from the University of Oxford (~2000–2004). He founded Oxford Buddha Vihara and Shan State Buddhist University, holding posts at Oxford, ITBMU, and Oxford Buddha Vihara.
Khanderao Deshpande was an Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies under Moriz Winternitz. He served as Joint Director at Osmania University (attested 1969).
Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk (1938–2014) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.
Khen Gen Jampal Dorjé studied under teachers Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery. He served as a professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling (attested 1995), and taught Kevin A. Vose and Lobsang Tendzin.
Khenchen Ngawang Khyen Rab Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche (1938–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Gochen and Riwoche monasteries under Dudjom Rinpoche and others, later chairing the Nyingma section at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1984).
Khenchen Tashi Özer studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye. He taught Khakyab Dorje and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (1933–2023) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Khenpo Gangshar and the 16th Karmapa, served as Abbot of Rumtek Monastery (~1976) and Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981), and founded Thrangu Tashi Choling Monastery.
Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Khenpo Appey Rinpoche (1927–2010) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dzongsar Monastery under Drakgyab Lodrö. He served as Director of Sakya College (1972–1985) and held a post at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.
